Fetch public-inquiry records from Luxembourg.

Source: R/get_assessments_lu.R
get_assessments_lu.Rd

Implementation of get_assessments() for Luxembourg. Backed by the national public-inquiry portal (https://enquetes.public.lu, "Enquêtes publiques"). Records are listed through the portal's own anonymous JSON search endpoint (/ctie/searchresults, 21 items per page) and enriched from each inquiry's detail page (parsed with rvest). Language is French (fr); portal-native values are kept verbatim.

Usage

get_assessments_lu(
  date_range = NULL,
  limit = Inf,
  download = FALSE,
  cache_dir = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  max_file_size_mb = NULL,
  write_sidecar = TRUE,
  refresh = FALSE,
  topic = NULL,
  relevance_threshold = NULL,
  relevance_model = NULL,
  query = NULL,
  theme = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

date_range, limit, download, cache_dir, overwrite, max_file_size_mb, write_sidecar, refresh, topic, relevance_threshold, relevance_model

See get_assessments().

query

Optional free-text query, matched client-side as a case-insensitive substring of the record title.

theme

Optional native theme slug: one of "etablissement", "gestion_eau", "environement" (sic), "agriculture", "amenagement", "energie", "patrimoine", "autres".

...

Reserved for future extensions; unused arguments are warned about.

Value

A tibble; see get_assessments() for the required schema.

Scope

all inquiries, not only EIAs: The portal lists every public inquiry (about 2,100 since 2020: classified establishments, water permits, environment, ...). The handler returns all of them by default and keeps the native theme(s) (theme, theme_label, theme_tags) and inquiry type (survey_type) as columns. The portal has no native "EIA report" flag, and the handler does not guess which inquiries are EIAs from title keywords: assessment_type is NA. Filter on the native theme (for example "environement", the portal's spelling) or on the title (query) instead. Only the "environement" theme (about 57 inquiries) mixes EIAs with Natura 2000, plans and permits; most classified-establishment and water inquiries carry no EIA report.

Listing and completeness

The search endpoint needs a constant data-id that the handler reads from the <cmp-search-results> element of /fr/enquetes.html (never hardcoded). Pages are requested from 1 until an empty page or until the reported totalMatches is reached; ids are de-duplicated and the number of UNIQUE ids is compared with the total. A malformed envelope or a failed first page is an error; a failed, short, empty-too-early or repeated later page, three consecutive failed pages, or fewer unique ids than the total (the warning names ids listed more than once, which suggests a shifted listing) raise a planscanR_warning_partial instead of returning a silently complete result. Known case: the portal lists inquiry 1041 twice, so a full crawl of all themes warns that one fewer unique inquiry than the total was retrieved (e.g. 56 of 57 for the "environement" theme). Inquiries closed or archived since about 2020 remain listed; earlier ones are not on the portal.

Records

document_id is "lu_" plus the native inquiry id (stable, also the last number in the title). Every native listing field is kept in the listing_json column (the raw search item). date_published is the opening date and date_close the closing date (both as shown on the detail page; the listing's timestamps are shifted by one or two hours); date_decision is NA (the portal exposes no decision date). competent_authority is the authority organising the inquiry (as written on the page; several are joined with "; "), supervising_authority the authority following the file, jurisdiction the municipalities. proponent is the requester ("Requérant : ...") line of the description when the page has one and it is not a private person (lines starting with a personal title such as "Monsieur" become NA), else NA. Also kept: native_id, reference_number, status_native, survey_type, nb_contributions, last_modified_native, procedure_type, municipalities_concerned, neighbouring_municipalities, related_links (opinions and meetings linked from the page) and every text section of the page in detail_sections (JSON). No geometry (locations are municipality names only).

Attachments

The detail page is fetched for every returned record (sidecar-first; a record whose detail fetch failed, or whose page looks unexpected, e.g. the few listed items whose page returns 404, is returned as a listing-only record (detail_fetched = FALSE: title, theme, status, dates, municipalities, reference number and listing_json, no attachments) with a planscanR_warning_partial; it is not cached and is retried next run, except a page that returns HTTP 404 (about 330 listed inquiries): that listing-only record is cached with detail_not_found = TRUE and only rechecked with refresh = TRUE). Every file link on the page (host *download.public.lu) is captured with its native label, grouped by the portal's own grouping into attachment_urls_<slug> columns: the accordion headings (normally fichiers), the per-case "Tout télécharger" archive (tout_telecharger, a zip that duplicates the other files) and links embedded in the description (description, for example a 7z dossier). Native labels per slug are in attachment_labels_native. Zip and 7z files are downloaded as-is, never unpacked, and bounded by max_file_size_mb (oversized files are reported as skipped_size); the main EIA report is often inside a zip.

Filter coverage

theme (a native theme slug, see get_assessments_coverage(); sent to the portal and re-checked client-side), query (case-insensitive title substring), and date_range (against the opening date of the listing, the same calendar day as date_published) are applied before the detail fetch; limit caps the result. Requests are throttled to 5 req/s (getOption("planscanR.lu_throttle_rate")).

See also

get_assessments(), get_assessments_coverage().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
get_assessments_lu(theme = "environement", limit = 3, download = FALSE)
} # }
